page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, with 4 physical cores and a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 80 GB NVMe SSD. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this server configuration.

Benchmark data indicates average performance for standard CPU tasks but highlights some limitations in memory bandwidth and specialized workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng falls into the average category, with scores of 1777.99 and 7055.54 respectively. However, memory bandwidth is mixed; while large block read and write speeds are average at 45.11 GB/sec and 26.08 GB/sec, small block cached reads are weak at 275.77 GB/sec. Geekbench scores are generally weak, including a single-core score of 1005.0 and a multi-core score of 3335.0. Cryptographic and image processing tasks show poor performance, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 637.38 and Geekbench image processing at 1893.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cax21 offers a resource-dense entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, utilizing shared CPU resources to maintain a low hardware-class profile. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under sustained high loads. Additionally, the weak memory performance and lack of advanced vector or matrix extensions limit its suitability for intensive mathematical or AI workloads, such as LLM inference where prompt processing on a small 135M model registers a poor 169.73 tokens/sec.

This server is best suited for lightweight, scale-out workloads that benefit from ARM architecture. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development and testing environments, lightweight database operations, and simple utility scripting. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications, heavy cryptography, or machine learning tasks.
